title: Fouling mechanisms during ultrafiltration of corn steep liquor: a combined blocking model and rheological analysis

record.title: Fouling mechanisms during ultrafiltration of corn steep liquor: a combined blocking model and rheological analysis
record.abstract: Corn steep liquor (CSL), a by-product of wet-milling, was subjected to ultrafiltration with 10 and 30 kDa polyethersulphone membranes at TMP values of 0.5–3.0 bar to characterise fouling mechanisms. Hermia's blocking models (complete, intermediate, standard blocking and cake filtration) were fitted to flux–time data. Cake filtration was the dominant mechanism at protein concentrations above 15 g/L and TMP above 1.5 bar, while intermediate blocking prevailed at lower concentrations. Dynamic viscosity of the feed ranged from 3.2 to 18.7 mPa·s depending on solids content, and cake compressibility index was determined to be 0.61, indicating a moderately compressible deposit. Backwash at 0.5 bar for 30 s every 15 min restored 70–85% of initial flux. The study provides design parameters for ultrafiltration as a clarification step in CSL-based fermentation medium preparation.
